title: Clonal expansion within pneumococcal serotype 6C after use of seven-valent vaccine.
ehr_evidence: Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from children aged four years and under with written parental/guardian informed consent... All serotype 6C invasive disease isolates (n = 4) from blood or cerebrospinal fluid specimens received by the HPA South East regional microbiology laboratory between 2006 and 2010 were included
summary: Genomic epidemiology study investigating clonal expansion and genetic diversity of Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 6C following PCV7 vaccine introduction in Southampton, England.
key_findings: Serotype 6C carriage increased fourfold from 3.8% in 2006/7 to 13.5% and 13.7% in subsequent winters.
The largest clonal complex (CC395) comprised 12 isolates and was uniquely characterized by a lantibiotic synthesis locus.
Single nucleotide polymorphisms separating isolates from the reference strain ranged from 8 to 19,829, with up to 172 SNPs within the CC395 clonal complex.
One carriage isolate (SOT2029) showed resistance to erythromycin and tetracycline and carried ermB and tetM resistance genes.
Two invasive isolates clustered together despite being collected two years apart, indicating persistence of a virulent clone.
study_design: Genomic epidemiology study using whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic network analysis
population: Children aged ≤4 years (carriage) and adult patients (invasive disease) in Southampton, England
limitations: Cross-sectional collection limits temporal causal inference
